result.title: When Does Reusing Layers Help Multimodal Embeddings?
result.summary: We ask whether a compact universal multimodal embedding models can produce better search embeddings by running the same layers again. Looped transformers add computation with nearly unchanged model size, making them an appealing alternative to a larger encoder. Their success in language-model reasoning and recent use for retrieval motivate the idea, but higher retrieval scores alone do not reveal what an extra pass contributes. We study eleven loop designs and training variants on three checkpoints of one vision-language architecture. Our protocol distinguishes whether a model uses its extra pass, whether its image states respond to the query, and whether those updates improve retrieval. We prove that an image placed before the query remains query-independent through repeated layers when information only travels forward. We then open a query-to-image path in three ways, including order-alternating recurrence, which places the query first on the next pass. Each path produces query-sensitive image states. For bidirectional attention and order alternation, freezing later visual updates does not lower accuracy. On all 78 datasets of the Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark version 2 (MMEB-V2), a standard added loop loses 0.46 points against its trained control; an intermediate generative stage changes the effect to +0.36. A model pretrained with recurrence gains +4.23 points over its own loop-removed control and benefits from query-conditioned image updates when answering visual questions or locating objects from text.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在同一视觉-语言架构的三个检查点上比较十一种循环层设计与训练变体，用「是否用到额外一遍、图像状态是否随查询变化、更新是否提升检索」拆解复用层的作用，并在 MMEB-V2 上报告混合收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其循环计算、查询到图像的信息通路与状态更新诊断，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 循环是否真正被使用、视觉状态是否受问题调制；但检索场景与推理仍有距离。
